newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude off as API data adopts bearish tone.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude off as API data adopts bearish tone.

text.p: NYMEX crude fell Wednesday afternoon, giving up early gains, after recent oil inventory data adopted a bearish tone as traders focused on stock builds in gasoline and crude.
"First the market was saying the crude builds were not that bad, but some traders always sell on stock builds no matter what," said a New York crude dealer.

At 1246 EST, February crude was off 27 cents a barrel at $24.84. Crude's declines triggered sell stops below $24.95, taking prompt crude to a session low of $24.65. February gasoline was off 0.49 cent a gallon at 66.55 cents.
On Tuesday, the API said gasoline stocks grew 415,000 barrels compared with expectations of a build of more than two million barrels for the week ended January 10.

But, the Department of Energy's (DOE) Energy Information Administration (EIA) said Wednesday that gasoline stocks rose 1.8 million barrels. Crude stocks also grew, rising a large 4.7 million barrels, the API said.

Meanwhile, February heating oil was off 0.22 cent a gallon at 69.20 cents. Distillate stocks, which are comprised of heating oil and diesel, fell 1.3 million barrels, just about matching expectations.
But, dealers noted that the API report showed the distillate stock shortfall versus year ago has narrowed to a mere 350,000 barrels from almost 20 million last August.
"I still think the big API 'news,' and it was predictable a week or two ago, is that the great No.2 LSD (heating oil) deficit is now gone," said a trader in Texas.
Dealers shrugged off news the Houston Ship Channel was shut Wednesday morning as a heavy fog blanketed the area, delaying four inbound and four outbound deep-draft ships, shipping officials said.
"It's probably just a temporary situation," said one crude dealer, adding "Crude fell after failing at the $25.40 level, and that's what brought it down technically."
Technical support for prompt crude was pegged at around the $24.65 session low, echoing previous consecutive session lows by Feb crude December 23 and 24.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk +1 212-859-1761))
